body: @Caselit / @bryanforbes  - this is from #9217.   I *knew* something would break

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**generalize adapt_on_names to expect non-named elements** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4436

> @CaselIT / @bryanforbes - this is from #9217. I _knew_ something would break

strange that 1.4 worked when. is it connected to some other change in the 2 series?
well yes, the ORM DML feature.  but also I identified a variant of the #9217 case using column_property() that was broken too , that's likely broken in 1.4 also

issue.title: RETURNING with UPDATE syntax (PostgreSQL) not working as expected when column_property() is used

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When we map some ORM column attributes using `column_property()`, it works as expected when executing `SELECT` statement. However, using the  RETURNING with UPDATE statement will throw an `AttributeError` (see error stack below).  The only workarounds that I found are either:
1.  Set `deferred=True` to every `column_property()` definition.
3.  add `load_only` options to the statement by loading only the "real" columns of the underling table (see code sample)



Other observations:
1. Forcing to load the mapped columns (expressed by `column_property`()) using `undefer` options does not seem to work (see code sample). 



### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected
1. https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/mapped_sql_expr.html#using-column-property
2. https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/queryguide/dml.html#using-returning-with-update-delete-and-custom-where-criteria

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.3.0

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

asyncpg

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 15.1

### Python Version

4.10

### Operating system

Linux (WSL2)

### To Reproduce

```python
from db import Base
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy import Integer, String, update
from sqlalchemy.orm import column_property, load_only, mapped_column, undefer

class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"
    id = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    firstname = mapped_column(String(50))
    lastname = mapped_column(String(50))
    fullname = column_property(firstname + " " + lastname)
    # fullname = column_property(firstname + " " + lastname, deferred=True) workaround-1



async def not_working(db: AsyncSession):
    stmt = update(Foo).values(firstname="New First Name").where(Foo.id == 1).returning(Foo)
    foo = await db.scalar(stmt)
    print(foo)  # it raise the error below


async def not_working_undefer(db: AsyncSession):
    stmt = update(Foo).values(firstname="New First Name").where(Foo.id == 1).returning(Foo).options(undefer(Foo.fullname))
    foo = await db.scalar(stmt)
    print(foo) # it raise the error below


async def working(db: AsyncSession):
    stmt = (
        update(Foo)
        .values(firstname="New First Name")
        .where(Foo.id == 1)
        .returning(Foo)
        .options(load_only(*[getattr(Foo, c) for c in Foo.__table__.columns.keys()]))
    )
    foo = await db.scalar(stmt)
    print(foo)
```
